title: Keys typed while a command prints output are neither lost nor reordered
why: A person types the next command while the last one still prints (a build, a log). Each key must reach the PTY in order while output streams the other way; one dropped, doubled or swapped key changes the typed-N line. The journey checks the producer still ran after Return, so the keys really went in during output.
source: everyday terminal use (holistic-quality.md 1: long-running output while you type)

steps.text: sh -c 'for i in $(seq 1 600); do echo r-$((i+1000))-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx; sleep 0.02; done; echo producer-$((600*2))-done'

steps.title: the producer runs in the foreground and its output streams
the producer still ran after Return: the keys went in during output
after the producer ends, the typed line runs exactly as typed: its computed output shows
